label: Compact Kahler Manifolds
notes: This lecture spans printed pages 96 through 102. We ask what topology a compact Kahler manifold is forced to have. Hodge theory replaces de Rham classes by harmonic representatives, the Kahler condition splits them by complex bidegree, and the resulting symmetries become hard tests that ordinary symplectic manifolds can fail.

label: Hodge Theory Recap
notes: On a compact oriented Riemannian manifold the star operator builds a codifferential adjoint to d, and the Laplacian is their anticommutator. Hodge proved every de Rham class has exactly one harmonic representative, so cohomology becomes a finite dimensional space of solutions of an elliptic equation. This is the engine everything else rides on.

label: The Kahler Refinement
notes: Walk through the three Laplacians. On a complex manifold d splits into dolbeault operators, each with its own Laplacian. The Kahler identities, which hold exactly when the metric is Kahler, force these three Laplacians to coincide up to a factor of two. That single coincidence is what makes harmonic forms respect complex bidegree.

label: Hodge Decomposition
notes: State the theorem carefully. Because the Laplacian preserves bidegree, the harmonic k-forms split into pieces of pure type p plus q equals k. Translating back through Hodge and Dolbeault isomorphisms gives the decomposition of de Rham cohomology into Dolbeault groups. Emphasize that this fails on a general complex or symplectic manifold.

label: The Hodge Diamond
notes: Draw the diamond live. Each lattice point is a Hodge number, arranged by bidegree, with degree increasing downward. Conjugation reflects it left to right, and Serre duality through the Hodge star rotates it by a half turn. Point out that summing each horizontal row recovers the ordinary Betti number for that degree.

label: Symmetries of Hodge Numbers
notes: Make the two symmetries precise. Complex conjugation sends a harmonic form of type p,q to one of type q,p, giving equality of the two reflected Hodge numbers. The real Hodge star supplies the antipodal symmetry. Together they pin down the diamond from less than half its entries and drive every numerical consequence below.

label: Hard Lefschetz
notes: Introduce the Lefschetz operator as wedging with the symplectic form. Its powers map cohomology up in degree, and the hard Lefschetz theorem says the k-fold power is an isomorphism from degree n minus k onto degree n plus k. This forces Betti numbers to increase up to the middle, the strongest constraint in the package.

label: The Kahler Package
notes: Collect the toolkit. The dd-complement lemma, often written with the conjugate differential, says forms that are closed and exact in the right senses differ by a doubly exact term. Together with hard Lefschetz and the primitive Lefschetz decomposition this is the package that no formal manifold can fake without genuine Kahler geometry.

label: Topological Constraints
notes: Spell out the obstructions a compact Kahler manifold must satisfy. Odd Betti numbers are even because the odd rows of the diamond pair up under conjugation. The class of the symplectic form is nonzero in degree two, so the second Betti number is at least one. These are checkable from cohomology alone.

label: Not Every Symplectic Manifold
notes: Deliver the punchline with the Kodaira-Thurston manifold. It is compact, symplectic, and complex, yet its first Betti number is three, an odd number. The Hodge parity test it fails proves it admits no Kahler metric. So symplectic strictly contains Kahler, and these tests are how we tell them apart.

label: Synthesis
notes: Tie the thread together. Compactness gives harmonic representatives, the Kahler condition splits them by type, the diamond encodes the symmetries, and hard Lefschetz amplifies them into Betti inequalities. The upshot is a battery of necessary conditions that separate Kahler, projective, complex, and symplectic geometry cleanly from one another.
